In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the methylene ATP derivatives are not metabolically stable and should not be used for any studies of purinergic receptor activation.

the effects of methylene ATP analogues on extracellular ATP levels in intact cells are complex and cell‐dependent and cannot be simply interpreted as reflecting the effects on ecto‐ATPases or ecto‐ATPDases.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
βγ‐me‐ATP is a substrate for eNDPKs but not for eNTPDAses and eNPPases.
βγ‐me‐ATP and α‐β‐me‐ATPP are not suitable tools for the analysis extracellular ATP metabolism, and that α‐β‐methylene‐ATP is the only suitable tool for this analysis.
methylene ATP derivatives are not metabolically inert and that their effects are cell‐specific.
The main takeaway from our work is that
methylene ATP derivatives can be used as probes to dissect the roles of eNTPD, eNPPs and eNDPKs, but that their effects on extracellular purine metabolism are complex and cell‐type specific.
methylene ATPs are not simply “metabolically stable” analogs, and their effects on extracellular nucleotide metabolism can be complex and cell‐dependent.
methylene ATPs are not inert, and they are not equally effective at blocking ecto‐ATPase activities in all tissues.
